text:
Pittsburgh won in a shootout, but the more interesting story is how thin the margin was and who kept it that way. Connor Dewar scored on a backhand early in the third period, a 5% chance by the model's reckoning, and that goal stood until Tyler Seguin tipped one in with 30 seconds left in regulation to make it DAL 1, PIT 1. Dallas had spent the third quarter of the game pressing, out-chancing PIT 1.29 to 0.54 in expected goals, and the late equalizer fit how that period went.

Before that, the game belonged to the home team. PIT led in shot attempts 68 to 54 and in expected goals 3.2 to 2.63 (2.29 to 1.34 at even strength), and the second period was the widest gap, 1.35 to 0.65. The reason it stayed 0-0 for so long was Jake Oettinger, who stopped 20 of 21 shots and saved 2.2 goals more than the chances against him deserved. Arturs Silovs was nearly as good at the other end, stopping 24 of 25 against 2.63 expected goals against. Both teams went empty on the power play, DAL 0 for 3 and PIT 0 for 5.

The shootout was close until the end. Ben Kindel and Sidney Crosby scored for PIT, with Seguin and Wyatt Johnston answering for DAL, and Egor Chinakhov was stopped in the third round. Rickard Rakell scored in the fourth, and Mikko Rantanen was stopped to end it. By the simulated replays of every shot, PIT deserved to win 60% of the time, so the result matched the balance of play, though not by much.
